items.prompt: White's a-pawn stands on a3 instead of a2; nothing else has changed. Does Rxg2+ still win for Black? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: Rxg2+ still forces mate in six or fewer.

hints: Compare this position with the one where the sacrifice worked. What exactly is different?
Does the a-pawn have any part in the attack on g2?
No.
items.explain: The a-pawn is a difference between the positions, but it plays no part in the attack on g2. Rxg2+ still forces mate in six or fewer.

items.prompt: White to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: The engine's first choice is this move.
It forces mate in 6 or fewer.

hints: Which king is easier to reach? Count the pieces aiming at it.
Which square can the rook reach with check, and where can the queen join it next?
items.explain: Black has the extra pawn, but the rook attacks g7 in front of the Black king and the queen can join it. Rxg7+ forces mate in six or fewer. A difference helps the side it favours, which is not always the side with more material.

items.prompt: Black to move. Name the target of the plan, then find the first move.

claims.statement: The engine's first choice is this move.
It forces mate in 7 or fewer.

hints: Which of Black's pieces already looks down the g-file?
The pawn in front of the White king is the target.
items.explain: White's king on g1 faces the rook on the g-file, and the queen can join it with check on g4, so Rxg2+ forces mate in seven or fewer. The plan has a target (the king) and pieces that can reach it.

items.prompt: White's king stands on h1 instead of g1. Does the sacrifice Rxg2 still work? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: Rxg2 is at least three pawns worse than the best move.

hints: Where is the king now compared with the position where the sacrifice worked?
What does the rook on g2 attack when the king stands on h1?
Nothing it can keep.
items.explain: With the king on h1 the sacrifice no longer works: Rxg2 is at least three pawns worse than the best move. A small change in king position changed the verdict.

items.prompt: White to move. In the earlier position the Black king stood on g8 and Rxg7+ won. Here the Black king stands on c8. Does Rxg7 still work? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: Rxg7 is at least three pawns worse than the best move.

hints: Which side of the board is the Black king on?
What does the Black knight on f6 attack?
White's queen.
items.explain: With the Black king on c8 there is no mate on the g-file, and Black's knight attacks White's queen on h5. Rxg7 is at least three pawns worse than the best move.

items.prompt: Black to move. White's king stands on c1. Find the best move.

claims.statement: The engine's first choice is Qxe4.
Rxg2 is at least three pawns worse than the best move.

hints: The king difference that made Rxg2 work is gone. Look for another difference.
Which White pawn is attacked by the queen?
The pawn on e4.
items.explain: With the king on c1 the attack on g2 is gone (Rxg2 is at least three pawns worse than the best move). A different difference decides: White's e4 pawn has no defender, and Qxe4 takes it while moving the attacked queen.

feedback_by_move.g8g2: The king is not on the g-file, so the sacrifice has no target.

claims.statement: The engine's first choice is Nxh4.
Nxh4 wins at least three pawns of material.

hints: Is this a quiet position where you need a plan?

The knight attacks the queen.
items.explain: A capture wins the Black queen at once, so no plan is needed: when something can be taken or threatened, calculate it first. Plans are for quiet positions.
